value.content: {"id": "portswigger_dom_vulns", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "dom_vulnerabilities", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: DOM-Based Vulnerabilities & DOM Clobbering", "name": "DOM-Based Sinks, Sources & DOM Clobbering Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-79", "owasp_category": "A03:2021 - Injection", "signals": ["window_location_source", "document_referrer_source", "innerhtml_sink", "eval_function_sink", "web_message_listener", "dom_clobbering_named_elements"], "verification_strategy": "Audit client-side JavaScript execution paths tracing data flows from tainted DOM sources (location.search, location.hash, postMessage) into execution sinks (innerHTML, eval, document.write, location.href). Test DOM clobbering using named HTML tags (id / name attributes on form, img, a tags).", "evidence_requirements": ["source_to_sink_trace", "clobbered_variable_name", "browser_js_callstack"], "tools": [{"tool": "BrowserAgent (DOM Inspector)", "cmd": "BrowserAgent.trace_dom_dataflow(url)", "desc": "Hooks DOM execution sinks and monitors taint propagation from URL parameters"}, {"tool": "katana", "cmd": "katana -u url -jc -kf all -headless", "desc": "Headless JS endpoint and script extraction engine"}], "remediation": "Avoid dangerous sinks like innerHTML and eval(). Use textContent, document.createElement, and safe DOM APIs. For postMessage listeners, strictly validate event.origin and event.source.", "description": "PortSwigger DOM vulnerability curriculum analyzes DOM XSS, DOM open redirection, DOM cookie manipulation, DOM clobbering overriding JavaScript global objects, and insecure Web Message (postMessage) handling."}
